explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The man says, “My daughter has just died…” and then he keeps going: “But come and place Your hand on her, and she will live.” He doesn't stop at the bad news. I think that takes more nerve than most of us have on a good day.

A fever would be a hard day, but that's not what he says. The synagogue leader tells Jesus, “My daughter has just died…” He's not asking Jesus to come fix a sickness. He's already past that, and he asks anyway.
No running away in this one, friend. The text has him say, “My daughter has just died…” Then he asks Jesus to come and place His hand on her.

True! He says, “But come and place Your hand on her, and she will live.” His daughter has just died, and he still says WILL live. I'd have been standing there with my mustache in a knot, and this man is giving Jesus directions.

Not false, friend. The man says it himself: “But come and place Your hand on her, and she will live.” He says it right after telling Jesus his daughter has just died. That "But" is doing some heavy lifting.
Not quite, friend. Matthew 9:19 says, “So Jesus got up and went with him, along with His disciples.” He doesn't put it off. He gets up and goes.
False is right! The text says, “So Jesus got up and went with him, along with His disciples.” A man kneels and asks, and Jesus gets up and goes.
Yes, the fringe of His cloak. She comes up behind Him and touches “…the fringe of His cloak.” Behind Him, just the edge. Bless her, I would have tripped and knocked over a whole bakery table.
Good guess if you're picturing a low reach, but no sandal here. Matthew 9:20 says she touched the fringe of His cloak. That's where her hand goes.
Close to His clothes, but not the belt. She touched “…the fringe of His cloak.” (Matthew 9:20). The cloak is what she reaches for.
Healed! She says to herself, “If only I touch His cloak, I will be healed.” Twelve years of bleeding, and her whole plan fits in one sentence. Short plan, big faith.

Forgiven is a wonderful word, but it's not hers here. She says to herself, “If only I touch His cloak, I will be healed.” She's been suffering from bleeding for twelve years, and healing is what she's after.

Blessed is a nice word, friend, but it's not the one she uses. The text has her say, “If only I touch His cloak, I will be healed.” After twelve years of bleeding, I think healed was the word on her heart.
Faith it is. Jesus says, “Take courage, daughter…” and then, “your faith has healed you.” The text says she was healed from that very hour. Not next week, not after a follow-up visit.
Twelve years of suffering is no small thing, friend. But Jesus doesn't say patience. He says, “your faith has healed you.” Then she's healed from that very hour.
Prayer is a good thing, but that's not the word Jesus uses. The woman says nothing out loud here. She only says it to herself, and Jesus tells her, “your faith has healed you.” (Matthew 9:21-22)

explanations.answer: She is not dead but asleep
explanations.explanation: Yes! Jesus says, “The girl is not dead, but asleep.” He says it to the flute players and the noisy crowd. And remember, her father had said she'd just died. Jesus is about to show what He meant.

explanations.answer: She will rise in three days
explanations.explanation: Not that one, friend. Jesus tells the crowd, “The girl is not dead, but asleep.” There's no waiting period in it. Matthew 9:25 shows Him going in and the girl getting up.

explanations.answer: She is safe with God now
explanations.explanation: That sounds comforting, but it's not what Jesus says. His words are, “The girl is not dead, but asleep.” He gives the crowd that one line, and then they laugh at Him.

They laughed. Jesus tells the crowd to go away, and then He says, “The girl is not dead, but asleep.” Right after that, the text says, “And they laughed at Him.” That's how the crowd answers what He says about the girl. Their answer is laughter.
There's plenty of noise in that house, I'll give you that. But the text says they laughed at Him. Jesus says, “The girl is not dead, but asleep.” and the answer is laughter.
Staring would've been quieter, friend. But the text says, “And they laughed at Him.” That's the crowd's reaction to what Jesus says about the girl.

explanations.answer: He takes her by the hand
explanations.explanation: Yes! Jesus “…went in and took the girl by the hand, and she got up.” Remember her father said, “…place Your hand on her…” Jesus takes her hand, and she gets up. This happens after the crowd had been put outside.
I can see why you'd picture that, but the text doesn't say it. Matthew 9:25 says Jesus “…took the girl by the hand, and she got up.” That's it. A hand, and she's up.

Her father is who asked Him to come, but the text doesn't show Jesus calling for him. It says Jesus went in and “…took the girl by the hand, and she got up.” (Matthew 9:25) Jesus does it with the crowd already put outside.
Not true, friend. Matthew 9:26 says, “…the news about this spread throughout that region.” The news did not stay inside. A girl gets up, and that news is out the door.
False is right! The text says, “…the news about this spread throughout that region.” It didn't stay in the house. It went out through the whole region.
